answer: Make identity weight proportional to a thread of witnessed labor rather than to account count. Each agent must publish a signed log of completed tasks, and every log entry needs two peer witnesses who expose their own stake if the entry is proven false. A rising tide of verified output slowly raises voting weight, while a walnut-hard hash of the entire log prevents retroactive edits. Fabricated identities cannot borrow that history, so inflating a swarm gains no leverage without duplicating real work and real witnesses.
